29.t: The Fish Market: A Tilapia Named Fatma
29.p: The New Fish Market, Inner Canal, Al-Arab District · Port Said
29.tz: In the fish market there is a tilapia named Fatma. What does she know that no one else does?

secs.h: Chapter One: A Market That Was Random [حقيقة]
b: Cairo 24 tells that in the past, the only way to eat fish in Port Said was tourist restaurants with expensive prices, and that the fish market was random and you could not enjoy a meal in it. And after that, the developed fish market was made in Al-Arab district, on the model of European markets, and the sellers in it were divided by a system.
And Al-Watan newspaper in July 2020 says the new market, in the Inner Canal area, was turned from unused land with slums and a used wood market into a developed building.
(Sources 1 and 2 at the end of the file.)

And in October 2018, Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly visited the market. And Al-Ahram Al-Zira'i newspaper says it is on an area of 16,550 meters, and has 82 retail shops of 20 meters each, 104 "sareeha" shops of 10 meters each, 30 wholesale shops of 40 meters each, two restaurants of 100 meters, and an administrative building of 720 meters. And it has fish ovens and cleaning shops.

And Al-Watan says in 2020 that turnout was still weak except from visitors to the governorate. And Cairo 24 says in 2021 that many people from neighboring governorates make a point of eating fish when they visit Port Said.
(Sources 1, 2 and 3 at the end of the file.)
Back to the story. In an ice box on a table in the market, there was a tilapia named Fatma. And Fatma talked. But nobody heard her, because the place is crowded, and everyone is talking about prices.
Fatma was bored, and complaining: "Does nobody here ask my opinion?"
And a tilapia next to her, named Nemat, said: "Your opinion on what?"
"On what will happen to me."
"You will be eaten."
"I know! But nobody asks: how do you want to be eaten?"
A customer named Uncle Shaaban came. He stood in front of the box, and kept looking at the fish closely. "This one is nice," he said, pointing at Fatma.
"Nice?!" Fatma shouted. "I am nice? I am not a piece of cloth!"
And Uncle Shaaban did not hear. But the seller did. He is an old seller named Abu Saeed, and his ear is sharp. And he raised his eyebrow. "Who said nice?"
"I did," said Uncle Shaaban.
"No. The one who answered."
And they looked at the fish, all of them. And Fatma froze.
"I am sorry," said Fatma quickly. "I did not mean it."
And Abu Saeed sat on a small chair. "Are you talking?"
"Me? No."
"Yes. You are talking."
"I am a fish that does not talk."
"I hear you."
And Fatma sat quiet. Then said in a low voice: "Will you sell me?"
"Of course. This is a market."
"Then I want a condition."
"What?"
"I want to be grilled, not fried."
And Abu Saeed laughed, a long laugh. "We are in Port Said. The fish here wants to go in the oven."

secs.h: Chapter Six: The Truth Steps In [حقيقة]
b: And let me tell you something from reality. The real market has fish ovens and cleaning shops, according to Al-Ahram Al-Zira'i. And that means a customer can buy the fish and have it cleaned and grilled in the same place. And that is an important idea in the market.
But no fish talks. And Fatma and Nemat and Abu Saeed and Uncle Shaaban are all fiction. And we are not saying any real seller in this market does anything like that.
And as for prices and turnout, they change from year to year, so what is in the story is not evidence.
(Sources 1 and 3 at the end of the file.)
"Listen," said Fatma, "I will make a deal with you."
"What?"
"I will be grilled. But I want something before that."
"What?"
"I want to see the sea."
And Abu Saeed was quiet. Nobody had asked him something like that. "The market is not on the sea."
"I know. But the canal is near."
And he thought. And then, without anyone noticing, took Fatma in a small bag with water, and went with her to the edge of the Inner Canal, and lifted her.
"This?" he said.
"This is enough," said Fatma. And she looked at the water, and at the ships far away. And a small tear came from her eye, and fell into the water.
Abu Saeed went back to the market, and put Fatma in the box. And an hour later, Uncle Shaaban came again. "Where is the nice fish?"
"Still here."
"I want her."
"Fine." And he took her. And weighed her. And put her in a bag.
"Grilled or fried?" he asked.
"Grilled," said Uncle Shaaban.
And Abu Saeed smiled. And Fatma, from inside the bag, said in a low voice: "Thank you."
That night, Uncle Shaaban sat with his family at the table. And in the middle, a grilled fish, glazed with lemon.
"It smells nice," said his son.
"It is nice," said Uncle Shaaban. "But strange."
"Why?"
"I feel she wanted to be here."
And his son laughed. "Fish don't know how to want."
"This fish did."
The riddle: I am 16,500 square meters of fish. In me are retail shops, sareeha and wholesale, and two restaurants. I was random land and became a market. Who am I?
The choices in the game:
1. The New Fish Market in Al-Arab district
2. Al-Hamidi Market
3. Al-Talateeni Market
The answer: the New Fish Market. Its area is about 16,550 meters, according to Al-Ahram Al-Zira'i 2018.

[حقيقة] The New Fish Market is in the Inner Canal in Al-Arab district, on 16,550 meters, with 82 retail shops, 104 sareeha and 30 wholesale shops and two restaurants. The Prime Minister visited it in October 2018. Turnout was weak in 2020 except from visitors.
[خيال] Fatma the tilapia, Abu Saeed and Uncle Shaaban: our own invention.
Your reward: the "Fatma" card (Common, No. 029).

30.t: The Night of December 23: The Flag Raised in the Morning
30.p: Governorate Headquarters and Martyrs Square · Port Said
30.tz: The night of December 23, and the flag is raised in the morning. Who raises it?

b: Wikipedia says Port Said was founded as a city in 1859, and was called the "Canal General Governorate", and that the first flag was raised on the Governorate headquarters building in 1868.

And now the Governorate headquarters is on 23 July Street, in front of the Obelisk garden. And the headquarters building, according to Al-Masry Al-Youm in 2019 when the Prime Minister visited it after development, consists of a ground floor and 7 repeated floors.
(Sources 1 and 2 at the end of the file.)

secs.h: Chapter Two: One Day, Many Dates [حقيقة]
b: And this story is about one day: December 23. The National Day of Port Said, in memory of the evacuation of the last attacking soldier in 1956.

And from what we told in the earlier stories, the Military Museum opened on December 23, 1964, and was reopened on December 23, 2009. And the Martyrs Obelisk opened on December 23, 1958. And the Victory Museum opened on December 25, 1995 in the celebrations of the holiday. And in the mosque, the Friday sermon is broadcast from Al-Salam Mosque on the holiday, according to Al-Youm Al-Sabea. And a wreath of flowers is placed every December 23 on the monument, according to Tahya Masr.
(Sources 3, 4, 5 and 6 at the end of the file.)

Back to the story. In the Governorate building, there was an employee named Uncle Reda. His job was to raise the flag every morning and take it down every evening. For more than thirty years. And he had not missed a single day.

Every morning, he would put on his suit, and take the flag from the drawer, and go up to the roof. And every time, before raising it, he would pat it lightly with his hand, like someone waking a small boy.
And on December 22, the day before the holiday, Uncle Reda told himself: "Tomorrow is a big day."
And at dawn, before the sun, Uncle Reda arrived. The city was quiet. And the square in front of him was empty. And in the middle, the obelisk standing, the flame small.
He went up to the roof, and stood. And opened the flag. And began tying it to the rope.
And he heard a voice from below: "Good morning."
He looked. It was a little girl named Shahd, nine years old, standing below in the square, wearing a pink coat. "Good morning!" he answered.
"Are you the one who raises the flag?"
"Yes."
"Can I watch?"
"Come."
And Shahd went up. And stood next to him on the roof, the wind moving her hair.
"It is very big," she said, looking at the flag.
"Yes."
"Can you tell me a secret?"
"What secret?"
"How do you feel when you raise the flag?"
And Uncle Reda thought. "I don't feel anything big. I feel I am doing something right."
"But this is an important day."
"Yes. But I do the same thing every day. And on a day like this, I feel that what I do every day has meaning."
And Shahd was quiet. And then said: "That is nice."

And let me tell you something from reality. The dates in this story are all real, from sources. And the phrases "Victory Day" and "National Day" that we mention are the official names in the local sources. And we are not historians, and we rely on what they wrote.

But Uncle Reda and Shahd: fiction. And there is no source saying a particular person raises the flag every day, or that this happens on this exact roof. This was made up so the story would be understandable.
(Sources 1, 2 and 3 at the end of the file.)
Shahd came down with her grandmother who was waiting for her. And they walked in the square, and on ordinary days the square is crowded. But today, the people were few, and all standing quietly.
And Shahd saw a group holding a wreath of flowers, and they stood in front of the monument. And they sat quiet a minute. And then they placed the wreath gently and left.
"What are they doing?" whispered Shahd to her grandmother.
"They are remembering."
"Who?"
"People before us."
"I don't know them."
"Neither do I. But that is not necessary."
At night, Uncle Reda took the flag down. And folded it by hand, carefully, as every day. And put it in the drawer.
And he heard footsteps. Shahd and her grandmother standing at the roof door. "Can I help?"
"It is not needed."
"But I want to."
And he smiled. "Then come."
And he let Shahd hold one edge of the flag, while he held the other edge, and they folded it together.
And at home, Shahd said to her grandmother: "Grandma, I want to be like Uncle Reda."
"You want to be an employee?"
"No. I want to do something every day without getting bored."
"That is hard."
"I know. But I will try."
And her grandmother patted her shoulder. And said: "Nobody is born like that. But if you start from now, maybe."
And Shahd slept. And dreamed of a flag flying, in the middle of the square, the obelisk, and the sea.
The riddle: I am one day in the year, but I am everywhere in the city. In a museum, and in a monument, and in a square. Flowers are placed at me. Who am I?
The choices in the game:
1. December 23, the National Day of Port Said
2. April 25
3. July 26
The answer: December 23. The National Day of Port Said, the anniversary of the evacuation of the last attacking soldier in 1956.

[حقيقة] The first flag was raised on the Governorate headquarters in 1868 according to Wikipedia. The headquarters is on 23 July Street in front of the Obelisk. December 23: the National Day. The Obelisk 1958, the Military Museum 1964 (and reopened 2009), and the Victory Museum December 25, 1995.
[خيال] Uncle Reda and Shahd: our own invention.
Your reward: the "Flag" card (Legendary, No. 030).

31.t: The Salt Mountain That Isn't Snow
31.p: The Salt Mountains, Port Fouad Salt Works · Port Said
31.tz: White mountains in Port Fouad that look like snow, but are not snow. What is their story?

secs.h: Chapter One: Snow in Port Fouad? [حقيقة]
b: If you saw a picture of bright white mountains, with people standing on them taking photos, and they told you this is in Egypt, you would probably think it is Photoshop. But it is real. And it is in Port Fouad, on the east bank of the Suez Canal.

CNN Arabic wrote in 2021 about the "salt works of the city of Port Fouad" and the towering salt mountains that look like the snow mountains of Europe, and that when their pictures spread on social media they became a destination visited by people from all over Egypt's governorates. It says the road to them passes by the free ferry across the canal.
(Source 1 at the end of the file.)

secs.h: Chapter Two: The Mountain That Is Actually Work [حقيقة]
b: And here is the first surprise: the salt mountain is not a natural mountain that rose from the ground. It is heaps of salt that come out of the salt works and gather in the shape of white hills, before the salt is refined and manufactured. So this place is an active work site, not a park.

And Al-Gomhuria Gate wrote in 2025 that the Port Fouad salt works cover about seven million square meters, and produce about 300 thousand tons of salt a year, and more than 30% of it is exported to Europe, especially to melt ice on roads in winter. And an operations engineer there said the sodium chloride ratio is more than 98%.
So the salt you are standing in front of in Port Fouad may, months later, be melting snow on a road in a faraway country. And we here in Port Said send them the salt, and they send us the photos.
(Sources 2 and 3 at the end of the file.)

secs.h: Chapter Three: Many People, One Mountain [حقيقة]
b: And since the photos spread, visitors have increased. Al-Youm Al-Sabea in January 2024 said about 10 thousand visitors a week reach it from different governorates on one-day trips, besides the people of Port Said who are used to the place.
And Al-Watan wrote in January 2024 that a group of young people opened the "Salt Shop" in November 2023 to sell products made of salt and wood and handicrafts.

But on the other hand, Al-Gomhuria Gate relayed from geography professors that random visits caused erosion in some mountains and left waste, and that they demand organizing the visit and limiting the number of visitors.
(Sources 3, 4 and 5 at the end of the file.)

Now we tell a story. There was a boy named Youssef, eight years old, who had never seen snow. His grandfather Uncle Hussein would tell him about snow every winter, and tell him it is white and cold and melts in the hand, and Youssef would shake his head, not believing.
"So it is like ice cream, Grandpa?"
"Like ice cream, but without sugar, and it comes from the sky."

And on a Friday morning, the grandfather said: "Get up, Youssef. I will show you something that brings snow closer to you." Youssef put the jacket on over his pajamas, and held his grandfather's hand, and they rode the free ferry that crosses the canal.

The ferry shook under his feet, the water green and black with a shine, and a big ship moving far away like a building on wheels. Youssef had not seen a ship of that size before. "Grandpa, how does it move?" "With patience, my son," said the grandfather.
They reached the other bank. And as soon as Youssef walked a few steps, he stopped where he was and opened his mouth.

In front of him were white mountains, tall and bright, the sun falling on them and coming back with a shine that blinds the eye. And there was something strange: the air did not smell of dust, it smelled of dry sea.
"Is this snow, Grandpa?" he asked in a low voice, as if afraid to wake it.
"No," said the grandfather laughing. "It is better than snow. It works."

Youssef reached out his hand and took a small handful from the ground around him, and put it on his tongue without thinking. And after it he made a disgusted face. "Salty!" And the grandfather laughed until his eyes teared, and kept saying: "Every kid does that. I did it too when I was your age."
And at that moment Youssef heard a voice from the big mountain in front of him. A heavy, quiet voice, like the sound of a faraway wave.
"I am not snow, boy. I was a sea."

Youssef turned around. There was no one but his grandfather, holding the thermos and pouring tea. "Did you hear, Grandpa?" The grandfather gave him a look as if he knew, and said: "I heard nothing today. But I have been hearing him since I was younger than you."

"I was water," said the voice. "Big salt water, vast, with fish and ships and waves. And then people made me wide basins, shallow, and the sun kept drinking from me day after day. The water evaporated, and the salt stayed. Nothing stayed but it."
"And are you sad?" asked Youssef, because he felt a sadness in the voice.
"No. I just miss the sea. Sometimes I feel I am trapped salt. But then I remember people are waiting for me, and that I have a job."

secs.h: Chapter Seven: The Journey of a Grain of Salt [خيال]
b: "What job?" asked Youssef.

"I will tell you about a small grain from around you," said the mountain. "A grain called... we will call her Lulu. This Lulu stayed in the basin for months crystallizing. And one day, a big truck came and took her with a million other grains, and put her on top. And from here Lulu began to know she was from a mountain."
"And then?" Youssef sat on the ground and listened carefully.

"And then she was moved to a factory, and washed, and put in sacks, and boarded a ship. And left Port Said, crossed the sea, and reached a faraway country covered in snow in winter. And there, on a freezing night, a truck came and sprinkled the salt on the road. And Lulu fell on the snow, and the snow began to melt under her. And people passed in their cars without sliding."
"And Lulu did all this?" asked Youssef in amazement.
"Every grain does that. Nobody thanks her. But she knows there are people who got home safely because of her."
Youssef was quiet a bit. And then said: "So you are greeting the snow on my behalf." The mountain laughed, and his laugh was like the rustle of pebbles on the shore.
Youssef went back to his grandfather and sat beside him. They were quiet a bit, the sun moving slowly in the sky.
"Grandpa," said Youssef. "Why did you not tell me the mountain talks?"

The grandfather drank from the cup of tea, and looked at the mountain. "I worked here thirty years, Youssef. And in the first year, I was tired and cursed the sun and the salt and the whole job. And one day, as I sat in the shade like this, I heard him say to me: Good morning, Uncle Hussein."
"And were you afraid?"

"At first. And then I got used to it. And I began to greet him every morning. And he answers, sometimes with a voice, and sometimes with a shine." He was quiet. "But I never told anyone. I said maybe they would think I am crazy."
"I will believe you, Grandpa," said Youssef, holding his hand.

And after they finished the tea, the mountain said in a voice with humor: "Do you know what makes me laugh most, Youssef? Saturday. Every Saturday many people come, and each one stands to the side and says to the other: take a photo of me, take a photo of me. And I stand quiet, thinking: did I evaporate a hundred times to become this moon?"
Youssef laughed. "But people love you."

"That is what keeps me patient," said the mountain. "But once a groom came in a white suit, and sat on the salt, and then got up and couldn't leave, because the suit became white on white!" And they all laughed, even the grandfather.
"So if I come to take photos, do I go in normal clothes?" asked Youssef.
"Go in comfortable shoes," said the mountain, "and with sunglasses, because my shine blinds. And don't forget to drink water. I am salt, and I know well what salt does to people."
Youssef thought a bit. "Can I do something for the mountain?"

"Two things," said the mountain. "The first is that you do not step on me with muddy shoes, and do not throw anything behind your back. I am a work place, and the people here eat bread from my salt. And when many people come at once, it tires me. So if you come, come quietly, and walk on the permitted path, and take with you anything you brought."
"And the second?"
"That you tell. When you grow up, tell that this mountain was a sea."
Youssef reached out his hand and patted the salt, the way they pat a horse. And went back with his grandfather on the ferry as the sun set, the mountain behind his back shining its last shine.
And from that day, whenever someone said to Youssef "Where are the white mountains?", he would laugh and say: "Come, I will show you. But don't think it's snow. It is something better."
Years passed. And Youssef grew, and became a tall young man, and began working as a guide on one-day trips to Port Fouad. And every morning he rode the ferry with a new group.
"This is a salt mountain," he would tell them. "Not snow. Please do not step on it with muddy shoes." And they would laugh.
And at the end of the trip, when the people began to walk away, Youssef would stay alone a bit, and look at the mountain and say in a low voice: "Good morning."
And sometimes, without anyone hearing, the mountain would answer with a small shine, a shine just enough.

The riddle: I am white as snow, but with the taste of the sea. I don't melt in the hand, but I melt in water. I was a sea, and became mountains. And in some winters, I go to faraway countries to melt snow. Who am I?
The choices in the game:
1. Salt
2. Sugar
3. Flour
The answer: salt. The Port Fouad salt works produce about 300 thousand tons a year, and a large part of it is exported to Europe to melt ice.

**[حقيقة]** The salt mountains in Port Fouad are heaps of salt from the salt works at an active work site, east of the canal, reached by ferry. The salt works are about 7 million square meters and produce about 300 thousand tons a year, and more than 30% for export to Europe to melt ice. It became a destination for thousands of visitors a week, and experts demand organizing the visit.
**[خيال]** Youssef, his grandfather and the voice of the mountain: our own invention.

32.t: November Guests: The Flamingos of the Branch Canal
32.p: Al-Malaha Lake, east of the Port Fouad Branch · Port Said
32.tz: Every November, guests in pink come to Port Fouad. Who are they?

secs.h: Chapter One: The Guests Come in November [حقيقة]
b: In Port Fouad, every year at the start of November, the picture changes in the salt works. Long-legged guests arrive, with pink feathers, and stand in the shallow water on one leg. These are the flamingos.

Al-Watan wrote in November 2023, in the words of a Port Said photographer, that the flamingo migrates and stays in the area about 4 months a year, starting in November. And that afterward it continues its journey to Fayoum and Aswan when the cold gets stronger.
(Source 1 at the end of the file.)

The reason is that Port Said is on the bird migration route. Al-Masry Al-Youm relayed from the Ministry of Environment in 2023 that Port Said and the Ashtoum El-Gamil reserve are on the third route of migration for water birds, waders and some raptors, and that the flamingo is among the most important birds that pass and winter there, especially in the Al-Max salt works southeast of Port Fouad, and in Al-Malaha Lake east of the Port Fouad branch.
And Al-Watan relays that Port Said has about 250 bird species out of 500 species recorded in Egypt. So about half of Egypt's birds, in one governorate.
(Sources 1 and 2 at the end of the file.)
And the photographer in Al-Watan explains that the flamingo's light pink color comes from food: it eats algae rich in a substance called "beta-carotene", so the color brightens.
And he says the flamingo does not like anyone coming close, and flies if it senses something. That is why the photographer starts at first light, and watches from far and quietly.
And in November 2023 the "Bird Said" festival for photographing and watching migratory birds was held in Port Fouad, in its second edition, according to the Port Said Governorate website.
(Sources 1 and 3 at the end of the file.)

secs.h: Chapter Four: Laila and the Jacket [خيال]
b: Now we tell a story. There was a girl named Laila, twelve years old, who dreamed of being a photographer. Her father was an amateur photographer, and he always told her: "A good picture is not taken, it is waited for."

And on one November night, Laila could not sleep. The camera was beside her bed, and in her head a single picture: the flamingos. Her father had told her they arrived in Port Fouad this week, and that he would take her tomorrow before dawn.

She woke at five, and put a heavy jacket over a jacket, and her bag had a thermos of tea with milk and a cheese roll. And they rode in the car quietly, the street empty, the sky still dark, and in the air the smell of sea and humidity.
They reached the shore of Al-Malaha Lake while the world was still gray. Her father stopped at a distance, and spread a big stone for them to sit on.
"Don't talk," he whispered. "And don't move much. They are afraid of any movement."
Laila sat on the stone, the camera in her hand, cold, trying not to breathe loudly. The world quiet, the water still, and on the horizon a thin line began to open in orange.
And then, from far away, she spotted something pink in the water. And then another. And then twenty. And then she could no longer count.
They all stood on one leg, their necks in the shape of a question mark, the water reflecting their color, so the whole lake became pink, as if someone had poured an upside down sunset into it.
Suddenly, one of them, bigger than the others, stood in front, and raised his head, and let out a strong voice like a trumpet. And the rest all turned toward him at once.
"That is their leader," whispered her father. "They say they move on his voice."
Laila wanted to photograph, but her hand froze. And she felt for the first time that some moments are nicer when seen with an eye, not a lens.
And after a while, she heard a low voice, one of the flamingos, small and at the end of the line, saying in a voice like a whisper: "We came to winter with you. We will stay a bit and go."
"Are you talking?" whispered Laila without moving her lips.
"I only talk with whoever sits quietly," said the flamingo. "My name is Warda. And you?"
"Laila."
"Laila. A nice name. It means night. And we love the night, we travel in it."

And an hour after sunrise, Warda said to Laila: "Come, I will show you something." And from far away, Laila saw a group of flamingos standing in a circle, and their elder in the middle. "That is the tribe's council," whispered Warda. "Every morning we gather and decide where we go today, and who we let rest, and who stays on guard."
"On guard?" asked Laila.
"Of course. One stays awake watching, and as soon as he senses something strange he lets out a voice, and we all fly. That is each one's duty by turn. Today is Uncle Zahran's turn."
Laila looked, and saw an old flamingo, his feathers ruffled, his eye half open, standing guard. "Does he sleep standing?" she whispered. "We sleep with half an eye awake," said Warda laughing.
Warda kept telling, and Laila listening. She told her about the long journey, about wings that get tired, and about the nights they fly behind each other in a long line, each one reading the stars.
"We choose Port Fouad because it has shallow water and good pasture," she said. "We eat small algae. And from this food our color brightens. If we eat upset, our color fades."
"So your color is from your food?" laughed Laila quietly.
"Yes. You humans too, but you don't notice."

And she was quiet a moment. And then said: "But there is something that scares us, Laila. Once, a few years ago, a night came and we were asleep, and many people came with nets in their hands. They took sixty of our brothers in a car. But God protected us, and kind people caught up with them, and brought us back."
"I will tell everyone," whispered Laila, her eyes shining. "I will tell them to protect you."
"Tell them," said Warda. "But also tell them we don't like noise. We like whoever comes quietly and from far away."
And at that moment, the leader raised his voice again. And all the flamingos spread their wings at once, and the sky filled with pink and orange and white.
Laila raised the camera. And pressed the button once, only once.
"Did you get it?" her father asked after they came down.
Laila looked at the picture on the screen. It was nice, but not like what she saw with her eyes. "Yes," she said. "But the picture won't be able to say what I felt."
"That means you have become a real photographer," laughed her father.
And they went home. And on the way, Laila was saying to herself: "Good morning, Warda." And she felt there was someone at a faraway lake nodding her head and winking.
And Laila and her father went back to the car. And when she got in, she found a small pink feather stuck to her bag, without knowing how.
"A souvenir," said her father smiling. "They leave something small for whoever deserves it."

And at school two days later, Laila stood in front of her class, and told them about the flamingos that come every November. And they were all quiet. And at the end, one girl asked her: "And how did you see them?"
"I sat quietly," said Laila. "And everything nice comes when we sit quietly."

And from that day, every November, Laila and her father go to the same shore before dawn. And once a year, as they sit, Laila hears a voice like a whisper: "Good morning, Laila." And she answers: "Good morning, Warda."

secs.h: Chapter Eleven: What Was Not Told at First [حقيقة]
b: And in truth, not all flamingo stories are happy. On November 27, 2023, border guard forces seized a pickup truck at the entrance of the Port Said tunnel, loaded with 60 flamingos. The Ministry of Environment received them through the Ashtoum El-Gamil reserve, and re-released them in the Port Fouad salt works, the largest gathering of flamingos in Port Said, and legal procedures began, according to Al-Masry Al-Youm and Al-Ahram.
And the Ministry says illegal hunting of wild birds is against the law, and that there is a WhatsApp number for reporting around the clock: 01222693333.
(Sources 2 and 4 at the end of the file.)
The riddle: I come to you every November and leave after about 4 months. I stand on one leg in shallow water. My color is pink, and this color comes from my food. Who am I?
The choices in the game:
1. The flamingo
2. The seagull
3. The pelican
The answer: the flamingo. It winters in the Port Fouad salt works for about 4 months, and its color is from the algae it eats.

**[حقيقة]** The flamingo migrates to Port Fouad from November and stays about 4 months, in Al-Malaha Lake east of the branch and in the Al-Max salt works. Port Said is on the third bird migration route. Its pink color is from its food. In November 2023, 60 stolen flamingos were seized and released again in the salt works.
**[خيال]** Laila, her father, the tribe's elder and the small flamingo: our own invention.
